Lead one shared practical-and-feedback task in P5, then one shared visit-planning task in P6. About ten pupils across BUILD, GROW and LAUNCH work in one room with the teacher and three TAs. Theme: Try, review and plan the visit. Planned full-day visit: a full day next term (date to be confirmed).

Confirm the practical route before the session

Owner selects kitchen trial bake OR cold finishing using accepted Lesson 7a instructions. Cold finishing of safely prepared stock is the default one-room route. A kitchen trial needs approved facilities, ingredients, individual allergy/dietary checks, hygiene, adult supervision and enough time for its actual safe process. Check the recipe, equipment, storage and cooling plan before starting. A separate kitchen needs a specifically approved change to the one-room plan; this pack does not authorise one. If unresolved, use the non-food panel/label task.

Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
P5 say and show

“We will practise one agreed food task and give useful feedback. GROW uses its existing practical instructions with an adult. The panel can choose a safe taste only after adult approval, or check a label, sample picture or presentation without tasting. You may pass. Tell us what you actually checked. We will tally real replies and choose one improvement to consider.”
Kitchen trial bake option

TA3 uses the accepted Lesson 7a method under the owner-confirmed food plan. Choose only a bounded step that can be finished and secured by reset. Do not invent a recipe, oven setting or bake/cool time to fit 25 minutes. Freshly baked food is not offered until the responsible adult confirms it is safe and suitable. If the new batch is not ready, panels can inspect labels or a separately approved, clearly identified prepared sample. Keep its feedback separate from the new trial.
Cold finishing option

TA3 uses accepted decoration/packaging or finishing instructions on safely prepared, suitable stock. Owner confirms ingredients, allergens, storage, clean tools and handling. Cold finishing still needs food controls. No compulsory handling or eating. If no suitable stock or approval is available, use a non-food label/pack mock-up and record practice.

13:00–13:20: teacher sets the shared goal and models one specific comment. TA1 and TA2 support two small feedback panels; TA3 supports the GROW practical station. Adjust groups to actual needs; the pathway split is not prefilled. Each pupil retains an own action. Pairs may share a role. Food, paper and personal items remain separate.

13:20–13:25: collect Keep / Change / Not sure replies, identify the feature and whether it was tasted or not tasted. Count only actual replies. A pass or absence is not automatically Not sure. Keep taste feedback separate from label/presentation feedback. GROW uses the real feedback to consider a justified improvement; no preference or successful bake is invented.
Reset from 13:25 to 13:35

Say “Stop, tools down, keep the tally.” TA3 secures food and equipment using the approved process; TAs clean and reset surfaces and count kit. Offer water, stretch or a quiet seated reset. Return to three mixed home teams for P6. No unattended hot work. If the practical cannot be secured safely, do not open the mock stall; staff adjust and record the unfinished work. Choose the cold or non-food option in advance when a safe finish cannot fit.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Staff answers and evidence checks
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A

Use actual approved practical records and actual panel replies. This pack adds no recipe, bake time, temperature or food production method. Kitchen trial or cold finishing is an owner decision using accepted Lesson 7a. If a safe process cannot fit the slot or checks are unresolved, use cold finishing if approved or a non-food equivalent.
Feedback tally worked model

FICTIONAL MODEL ONLY: four people comment on a pack picture, without tasting. Keep = 2, Change = 1, Not sure = 1. Total replies = 4. Tasted = 0; Not tasted = 4. This says nothing about flavour or the views of the other six pupils. No reply or a pass is not automatically Not sure.
Check
Sound interpretation
Four actual replies in this model, not ten tasters
Tasted / Not tasted
Keep the basis of feedback; never infer tasting
One clear comment
“Make the price easier to read” can guide a label change
Different preferences
Retain them honestly; a tally is not a food-safety decision
Practical evidence
Record the learner’s actual step and help, not a group achievement
Unfinished batch or rehearsal
Mark pending; do not assert completion
Kitchen or cold route

Both require adult checks of suitable ingredients, individual needs, hygiene, safe storage and handling. A cooked batch must be safe and suitable before release to the panel. Label a separately prepared reference sample clearly. Do not claim its feedback belongs to a new batch. A non-food inspection can give valid label/presentation evidence and is recorded as not tasted.
Quiet hinge

Privately ask or show: “Four pupils checked a label without eating. Can we record four taste scores?” No. Record four label checks, not tasted. If unclear, point to the tasted/not tasted field and model one honest entry before returning the task. No cold calling.
Staff answers and evidence checks continued
Thursday 12 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Enquiry is different from confirmation

Accept a scripted practice call or an unsent email draft with a clear purpose, planned date, group of ten pupils/four adults, useful questions and a polite close. The address, phone number, recipient and school name remain blank. No actual reply is supplied. Record a peer/adult rehearsal reply as practice, never as the venue’s response.

Useful questions cover winter opening and selected exhibits, group charges and what is included, short routes and surfaces, warm seated rests, toilets, lunch base, drop-off, shop access and the £5 pupil limit, permitted object photos, cancellation and booking steps. Teams may prioritise questions; do not make them read every one aloud.
Travel and kit answers

A sound plan works backwards from the owner’s latest return time, with outward travel, arrival, nearby stops, rests, lunch, optional shop and return. No journey duration or departure is invented. Kit can include warm/wet-weather layers, suitable footwear, lunch/drink, usual communication aid and approved shared recording kit. Adults hold medication and private contact information under the existing support plan.
Risk controls are planning questions

Cold or wet: suitable clothing, warm rests and an adult weather/route check. Fatigue: short walking sections, seated breaks and a route that works for the person who tires first. Separation: stay together, agreed regroup point and tell an adult. Food needs: adult checks meals and private dietary arrangements. Do not claim this pupil list is a completed visit risk assessment.
Station evidence stays with the accepted lesson

Use grow_community_cakesale_a2w2, L7a/L7b and L7-E1 from GCS-2_SEGMENT_E_issue3. The original two-page record captures practical work, checked pack/label, two rehearsals and money/cashless checks. Short appointments may leave elements unfinished. Keep those gaps and support visible; the Local Choice line indexes work and does not replace the full record.

Prompt ladder: point; short question; rephrase; scaffold or choice; model the first step only, then return the task. Routes are chosen by need, not fixed to pathway. Permit pass, pointing, exact scribing and private sharing. No sending, booking, payments or publication is performed.
